events.title: Shechem seizes and violates Dinah
events.narrative_summary: Dinah, Leah's daughter, goes out to see the daughters of the land. Shechem son of Hamor, prince of the land, sees her, takes her, lies with her and humiliates her.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word. Placed 5 years after Jacob's altar at Shechem (33:20), margin 3 years, so the window runs from 2 to 8 years after the altar (about 1906 to 1900 BCE on the linked dates, altar c. 1908 BCE): after the settlement at Shechem and before Joseph's 17th year (37:2), which is about 1899 BCE, about 9 years after the altar. Age arithmetic on the linked birth dates: Leah is married after year 7 of the service (29:20-23), so Reuben to Judah (four sons) come in years 8-11, Simeon and Levi about years 9-10, and Dinah after six sons (30:21), about years 13-14, a little before Joseph (30:22-25), born at the end of year 14 (evt.gen_30.joseph_born, c. 1916 BCE). Dinah is thus about Joseph's age and Simeon and Levi about 4-5 years older. At the altar (c. 1908 BCE) Joseph and Dinah are about 8, Simeon and Levi about 12-13. At the chosen window Dinah is about 10 to 16 (centre about 13) and Simeon and Levi about 14 to 21 (centre about 18). The text gives Dinah no age, only 'damsel' (na'arah, 34:3), so the window is an estimate and the later half suits both a marriageable Dinah (34:4) and sword-bearing brothers (34:25) better than the earlier half; hence MACRO_ERA. The outing and assault last a few hours.

events.title: Shechem loves Dinah and asks Hamor to get her
events.narrative_summary: Shechem's soul clings to Dinah, he loves her and speaks tenderly to her, and he asks his father Hamor to obtain her as his wife.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the assault directly (vayyomer, 'and he said'); no delay stated. Starts at the END of the assault with a one-day margin.

events.title: Jacob hears of Dinah's defilement and keeps silent
events.narrative_summary: Jacob hears that Dinah has been defiled. His sons are in the field with the livestock, and he holds his peace until they come.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No delay is stated between the assault and Jacob's hearing; anchored on the end of the assault with a one-day margin. The silence lasts until the sons return (34:7), which I estimate at some hours.

events.title: Hamor goes out to speak with Jacob
events.narrative_summary: Hamor, Shechem's father, goes out to Jacob to speak with him.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Anchored on the start of Jacob's silence with an offset of 4 hours (time to walk to the camp and for the sons' return to be possible), margin 6 hours.

events.title: Jacob's sons return from the field in fury
events.narrative_summary: When they hear what happened, Jacob's sons come in from the field. The men are grieved and very angry, because Shechem has done a disgraceful thing in Israel by lying with Jacob's daughter.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: They come 'when they heard'; placed at the end of Hamor's setting out, with a margin of 3 hours. The Hebrew does not fix their order relative to Hamor's speech.

events.title: Hamor proposes marriage and intermarriage
events.narrative_summary: Hamor tells them his son Shechem longs for their daughter and asks that she be given to him as wife. He proposes general intermarriage and offers them the land to live in, trade in and hold.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Continuous with the sons' arrival (34:8 'Hamor spoke with them'); starts at its end, a speech of about 20 minutes.

events.title: Shechem offers any bride-price for Dinah
events.narrative_summary: Shechem asks Dinah's father and brothers for favor and says he will give whatever they name as bride-price and gift, if only they give him the girl as wife.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Immediately follows Hamor's speech in the same meeting (34:11 'And Shechem said'); starts at its end.

events.title: Jacob's sons answer deceitfully and demand circumcision
events.narrative_summary: Because Shechem defiled their sister, the sons answer with deceit: they cannot give her to an uncircumcised man, but will agree if every male is circumcised, and then they will intermarry and become one people. Otherwise they will take Dinah and go.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The reply in the same meeting; the text gives no gap. Starts at the END of Shechem's offer with a margin of 3 hours for private conferring among the brothers.

events.title: Hamor and Shechem accept the terms without delay
events.narrative_summary: Their words please Hamor and Shechem. The young man, the most honored in his father's house, does not delay, because he delights in Jacob's daughter.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'He did not delay' (34:19): the acceptance follows at once; starts at the end of the brothers' terms.

events.title: Hamor and Shechem persuade the men at the city gate
events.narrative_summary: Hamor and Shechem speak to the men of their city at the gate. They call Jacob's people peaceable, urge intermarriage, and say the men will consent to dwell as one people only if every male is circumcised, adding that their livestock and property will become the city's.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the acceptance with no stated gap ('he did not delay'); a gate assembly lasting about an hour, margin 12 hours.

events.title: Every male of the city is circumcised
events.narrative_summary: All who go out of the city gate listen to Hamor and Shechem, and every male is circumcised.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the gate speech; the day of circumcision is counted as day 1 of the 'third day' of 34:25. Duration one day, margin one day since the text does not say how soon after the speech.

events.title: Simeon and Levi kill the males of Shechem and take Dinah
events.narrative_summary: On the third day, while the men are in pain, Simeon and Levi take their swords, come upon the unsuspecting city and kill every male, including Hamor and Shechem. They take Dinah out of Shechem's house and leave.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'On the third day, when they were in pain': counted from the circumcision as day 1, so offset 2 days from its start, margin 12 hours. Radak: the pain is greatest on the third day. Ibn Ezra: the third day is a hard day. Duration about 3 hours.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: On the third day, when they were in pain

events.title: Jacob's sons plunder Shechem and take captives
events.narrative_summary: The sons of Jacob come upon the slain and plunder the city because their sister was defiled. They take flocks, herds, donkeys, wealth, children and wives, and everything in the houses and fields.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the killing directly; the text gives no gap. Plundering a city and carrying off captives takes several hours; margin 6 hours.

events.title: Jacob rebukes Simeon and Levi; they justify themselves
events.narrative_summary: Jacob tells Simeon and Levi they have brought trouble on him by making him odious among the Canaanites and Perizzites. Being few, he fears they will gather and destroy him and his house. They answer, 'Should he treat our sister as a harlot?'
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Jacob's reaction follows the raid; no gap is stated. Anchored at the END of the plunder with a margin of two days for the sons' return to camp.

causal_edges.causal_explanation: The men of the city listen and are circumcised (34:24).
Jacob's sons plunder the city 'because they had defiled their sister' (34:27).
Jacob hears that Shechem has defiled Dinah (34:5).
Dinah's brothers Simeon and Levi (34:25) kill the males of Shechem for his violation of their sister, which they defend in 34:31: 'Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?'
Having taken Dinah, Shechem's soul clings to her and he asks his father to get her as a wife (34:3–4).
The sons answer deceitfully 'because he had defiled Dinah their sister' (34:13).
When the sons hear what Shechem did, they come in from the field, grieved and furious because he wrought folly in Israel by lying with Jacob's daughter (34:7).
The circumcised men are in pain on the third day, which lets Simeon and Levi attack unopposed (34:25).
With the males dead, the sons 'came upon the slain' and could spoil the city unopposed (34:27).
Jacob rebukes Simeon and Levi for the killings, fearing reprisal (34:30).
Shechem's request sends Hamor to speak with Jacob (34:6).
The terms of circumcision please Hamor and Shechem (34:18).
Having accepted, Shechem and Hamor go to the gate to persuade the men (34:19–20).
